title: WorkerMessage
description: One message on the worker <-> control-plane link. This is the COMPLETE vocabulary of that link: `type` is a closed enum and `additionalProperties:false` applies at every level, so there is no message that can carry a shell command, a Python expression, a filesystem path, or a bpy call. Every message carries protocol_version; job-related messages carry job_id and project_id so a receiver never has to infer scope. All network input is untrusted and is validated against this schema before anything else happens.

protocol_version.description: Incremented on any breaking change to this vocabulary.

token.description: Pre-shared worker token, present ONLY on worker_hello. Never stored by the control plane, never logged, never echoed in any other message.

job.description: A canonical Job. Deliberately NOT $ref'd to job.schema.json here: the envelope layer validates envelopes, and the Job contract is enforced separately by validate_job at BOTH ends. That separation matters — if a malformed job failed envelope validation it would be dropped as unparseable, and the control plane would never receive the explicit job_rejected explaining why. The control plane validates before offering; the worker validates again before accepting, because network input is untrusted.

worker_state.description: Liveness detail so the control plane can tell healthy-idle from healthy-busy.

job_status.description: duplicate means the job was already completed locally; the result is being reported, not re-executed.

execution_phase.description: Internal worker phase, for observability only. Never used as a contract.

result.description: Operation result payload, present on a succeeded or duplicate job_result.

preview.description: Reference to a preview artifact generated after the mutation was verified and saved. Only meaningful on job_result. Absent when no preview was produced; a preview is a REPORTING addition and never affects whether the mutation happened.

preview_error.description: Why preview generation failed, when the mutation itself succeeded. Reported SEPARATELY from `error` so the control plane never claims a design change failed after it was durably saved.

progress.description: Step progress within a multi-step plan, present only on job_progress. Carries what the browser shows while a reconstruction runs, so ONE reply can update in place instead of the transcript filling with one bubble per wall. The label is human-readable and free of internal identifiers by contract.

allOf.description: worker_hello must identify and authenticate the worker and declare capabilities.
worker_registered confirms the worker and states the heartbeat cadence.
heartbeat reports which worker and whether it is busy.
A job offer carries a canonical Job and nothing else about it.
Acceptance is explicit; socket delivery is not acceptance.
A rejection must carry a structured reason.
Progress is scoped to a job.
A result must state its status.
A failed result must carry a structured error.
Only worker_hello may carry a token.

Preview fields belong to job_result only. A preview says something about a completed mutation, so it is meaningless on a heartbeat, an offer, or a registration, and allowing it there would create a second place to look for artifact information.
A preview reference may only accompany a result that actually succeeded. Attaching one to a failed job would imply a picture of a change that was never applied.
